problem.title: Minimum Meeting Rooms
problem.statement: You have a list of meeting schedules (start time, end time). Calculate the minimum number of rooms needed so all meetings can run without conflict.
problem.hint: Each time a new meeting starts before another ends, you need a new room. When one ends, that room can be reused. Try sorting start times and end times separately.
problem.walkthrough:
Example meetings: [[9,10], [9,11], [10,12], [11,13], [14,15]].

Sort start times: [9, 9, 10, 11, 14]
Sort end times: [10, 11, 12, 13, 15]

Use 2 pointers:
9 < 10: meeting starts, need new room. Rooms = 1.
9 < 10: another meeting starts, need new room. Rooms = 2. (MAX)
10 >= 10: first meeting ends. Rooms = 1.
11 >= 11: second meeting ends. Rooms = 0.
11 < 12: meeting starts. Rooms = 1.
14 >= 13: meeting ends. Rooms = 0.
14 < 15: meeting starts. Rooms = 1.

Answer: 2 rooms.

Key insight: count how many meetings are active at the busiest time. That is the minimum number of rooms.
problem.solution:
def min_rooms(schedule):
    starts = sorted(s[0] for s in schedule)
    ends = sorted(s[1] for s in schedule)
    i = j = 0
    rooms = best = 0
    while i < len(schedule):
        if starts[i] < ends[j]:
            rooms += 1
            best = max(best, rooms)
            i += 1
        else:
            rooms -= 1
            j += 1
    return best
